name: bigcalc
algorithm: Evaluate the bigcalc dogfood's bench lines of big-number RPN with larger operands: a factorial's bit length, a Fibonacci number mod a prime, a Fermat test of a Mersenne prime by modpow, an integer square root, a gcd of two Mersenne numbers and a modular inverse; print each result (README.md).
notes: Tier A (M9 item 11.32): an Mk-only row, the bigcalc dogfood unchanged, compared across mk binaries; no twin, no peer, no defect line (README.md).

The lines are Dogfoods/bigcalc/cases/data/bench.rpn's, given to calc, which evaluates each argument as a line and then prints the top of the stack once more: the quick arguments keep the script's operands and print its bench.out and a last 443; the publish arguments raise them (3,000 to 30,000, 20,000 to 200,000, the Mersenne primes 2^4423 - 1 and 2^4253 - 1 to 2^19937 - 1 and 2^11213 - 1).
The size is provisional; tools/bench verify -publish-size fixes it in the quiet window, and the checksum changes with it.
